name: X-spider from H-boxes
summary: A phase-free X-spider is a Z-spider with arity-2 H-boxes on all its legs, up to a scalar.
description:
In the ZH-calculus the X-spider (the grey spider) is not a generator but is *defined* as a phase-free Z-spider with an arity-2 H-box on each leg, together with a scalar. This is the ZH version of the [colour change](../colour-change/) rule. Classically, the grey spider is the XOR.

The scalar here is for the PyZX normalisation of the X-spider, and differs from the one in the papers, where the grey spider is normalised so that it is exactly the XOR on basis states.
parameter_notes: n inputs and m outputs on the X-spider (shown for n = 1, m = 2); holds for any number of legs.

source.location: Section 2.1, definition of the grey spider

notes: The H-boxes here are *unnormalised*: an H-box with label $a$ has all entries equal to $1$, except for the entry where all wires are $1$, which is $a$. The grey spiders of the ZH papers are normalised differently from the X-spiders of PyZX, so scalar factors may differ from those in the papers.
